summary: Iter204 — verified Bundle Download (ZIP) endpoint + empty-state CTA pattern. Backend pytest: 12 passed / 1 failed / 1 skipped (safety-assessment skip, no /me record). Frontend: bundle button end-to-end works — clicking downloads a valid application/zip response (HTTP 200) with the correct purple→teal gradient, full-width layout, and descriptive helper text. Regression smoke on /login, /special-needs-v2, /dashboard all render without console errors. One backend concern: fresh throwaway parent receives HTTP 200 (with 2 always-available preview PDFs) rather than the expected HTTP 409, because /api/pathway-report/preview/pdf and /api/complete-report/mine.pdf always produce a placeholder PDF even for brand-new users.

minor.issue: Bundle NEVER returns 409 for a freshly registered user because /api/pathway-report/preview/pdf and /api/complete-report/mine.pdf always emit a placeholder PDF regardless of assessment state. Test expected 409 with a friendly nudge; observed 200 with a 2-file ZIP (pathway preview + complete alignment). Suggest: (a) exclude those two 'always-on' endpoints from the 'included' count when deciding 409, OR (b) have those endpoints return 409 when the user has no substantive data. The 409 code path in bundle_routes.py is currently unreachable for any authenticated user.

issues: Document has 12px horizontal overflow. Bundle button itself is well-sized (316px in 390px viewport); the overflow appears to be pre-existing decorative blur elements, not introduced by the bundle button.

rca of the issue: Bundle 409 unreachable: The _STATIC_ENDPOINTS catalog in bundle_routes.py (lines 64-105) includes /api/pathway-report/preview/pdf and /api/complete-report/mine.pdf. Both endpoints return valid PDF bytes even for a freshly-registered user (they render generic 'no data yet' placeholder PDFs, not 404/409). Because at least these two PDFs always end up in `included`, `if not included` at line 326 is never truthy → 409 branch dead. Fix options: (1) partition the catalog into 'always-on' vs 'gated', only count gated toward the readiness gate, (2) make those endpoints themselves return 409 when the user has no substantive data, (3) treat placeholder PDFs (identifiable by output length or a header) as 'not ready'.
